column2: 4.1. Strategic awareness

Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
column4: According to the documentation attached to the amendment to the Act No. 106/1999 Coll. re-use can be defined as the development of applications and services based on open data that are machine readable, with available metadata and legal openness. See https://www.psp.cz/sqw/text/tiskt.sqw?O=9&CT=222&CT1=0.

column2:
Are there any processes in place to monitor the level of reuse of your country's open data?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe these processes and (2) provide the URLs to support the answer.
column4:
In 2022 the National Open Data Team prepared an analysis for identification the level of the re-use of open data as a part of the analysis of the open data impact in the Czech Republic. There were at least 69 applications, portals and services based on open data identified. Moreover, according to the questionnaire sent out to all open data providers in December 2022, 15 (of a total of 56 that participated
in the questionnaire) providers regularly monitor the re-use of their open data. Results are published in the respective Annual Reports on the State of Open Data in the National Open Data Portal (https://data.gov.cz/výroční-zprávy/).
column7: The National Open Data Team annually prepares an analysis of the re-use of open data as a part of the analysis of the open data impact in the Czech Republic. At least 78 applications, portals and services based on open data were identified. Moreover, according to thequestionnaire sent out to all open data providers at the beginning of  2024, 22 (of a total of 67 that participated in the questionnaire) providers regularly monitor the re-use of their open data. Results for the year 2023 will be published in the Annual Report on the State of Open data on the national portal during the summer 2024.  Examples of 27 applications can be found on the  national portal https://data.gov.cz/aplikace.

column2:
Are there any activities in place to encourage public bodies to monitor the reuse of their own published data (e.g. incentives or obligations in place for public bodies or civil servants of national government)?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe these activities/incentives and (2) provide the URLs to support the answer.
column4: The National Open Data Team strongly encourage all public bodies to monitor the re-use of the data. Monitoring is required primarily for the Open Data Working Group members that subsequently have to report the results to the National Open Data Team through annual questionnaire about the state of open data in the Czech Republic. The results are available through the respective Annual Reports on the State of Open Data here: https://data.gov.cz/výroční-zprávy/.
column7: The National Open Data Team strongly encourage all public bodies to monitor the re-use of the data. Monitoring is required primarily for the Open Data Working Group members who subsequently have to report the results to the National Open Data Team through an annual questionnaire about the state of open data in the Czech Republic. The results will be available through the respective Annual Reports on the State of Open Data later in the summer 2024 here: https://data.gov.cz/výroční-zprávy/. There is a new feature on the national data portal where anyone can suggest an application that uses the open data. We are encouraging all our providers to upload their re-use solutions and applications they have for users. https://data.gov.cz/aplikace

column7: We have added a new specification that indicates the HVD datasets into the technical standard (https://data.gov.cz/ofn/) that is obligatory for all providers and that allow us to indetify what data are HVD. As all the applications in the catalogue (list of applications: https://data.gov.cz/aplikace) on the data portal are connected to the specific data set we can monitor also the reuse of the high-value datasets.

column2:
Has your government specified what 'impact of open data' means (e.g. in a strategy document)?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, how do you define the impact of open data in your country? 
* If possible, please provide a URL to a public document describing it.
column4:
The definition of the impact of open data is described in the Methodology for Developing an Analysis of the Impact of Open Data in the Czech Republic. The document was prepared as one of the objectives of the project KODI financed from the Operational Programme Employment and is published online https://data.gov.cz/kodi/. 
Impact of open data - Changes of the established ways of behavior and attitudes in the society through the values and services created on the basis of open data and their gradual implementation into the life of the society.

column2:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column4: The methodology is based on an indirect approach that is based on the identification of the value of open data across the whole of Czech society and takes into account various aspects such as the quality of open data, the existence of applications, data enrichment or benefits for providers.

column2:
Is there collaboration between government and civil society or academia to create open data impact in your country?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide an example
* If possible, URLs to such projects and collaborations.
column4: The collaboration between the government and the academia is embodied in the KODI project led by the National Open Dat Team and financed from the Operational Programme Employment where the majority of the team comes from the academic sector (ex. Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at the Charles University, Faculty of Law at the Masaryk University, or the Prague University of Economics and Business). All objectives of the project are available o the Portal:  (see Objective C3V11). Moreover there is a regular cooperation between the National Open Data Team and the NGO OSF Prague at the programme Our State, Our Data (see https://osf.cz/programy/ziva-demokracie/nas-stat-nase-data/) that supports the open data re-use in different projects and activities across the civil society in the Czech Republic.
column7: The collaboration between the government and academia is embodied in the NPO project (Czech version of the Recovery and Resilience Facility project) led by the Data Team until 2025. This project covers the development of the National open data catalogue as well as the data management activities. In the project participate representatives e.g. from Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at Charles University, Faculty of Law at Masaryk University, or Prague University of Economics and Business. Moreover, there is regular cooperation between the National Open Data Team and several civil sector communities e.g. https://www.czechitas.cz/, https://www.opencontent.cz/ as well as the informal community of Open Data Limo.

column2: Regular feedback sessions with portal users
column7:
The City of Prague organizes informal meetings with users of the portal and data once or twice a year. For example, thanks to the feedback they decided to unite several information websites about Prague data and reuse cases into one website to make it easier for users to find their way around and to be motivated to use the data.
Similarly, informal meetings are organized by the Digital and Information Agency. The ideas are than part of the development of the national portal. At the same time, DIA collects information for other public bodies as well.
Every year, the Region Hradec Králové organizes a hackathon for students and users to get feedback, at the last one was even created an application that facilitates the reuse of data on the portal and was directly implemented on the portal.

column2: Social media sentiment analysis
column7:
Digital and Information Agency follows the analysis of X account @otevrenadata where we communicate changes on the portal and we also called for participation in research for portal users.
Feedback from social networks (X) is also collected by the Ministry of Health, which regularly informs about currently published data and opens a discussion about what other items users would need (for example, data on diabetes or pregnancy). At the same time, they also present their own visualizations and get feedback on their quality and possibilities for further use.

column2: Other
column7:
The Open Data Team annually conducts a survey among the providers of the National open data catalogue. The providers are asked If and how they communicate with their users. Most of the providers do communicate with their users (13 out of 65). A most common way of communication is individual communication. Many of the regional providers also organize annual hackatons (usually together with the universities or NGOs) where they meet with the community of the users:  #HACKUJBRNO 2024, https://www.datakhk.cz/pages/hackathony, https://www.sitport.cz/kalendar-akci/infis-hackathon/, https://hackathon.upol.cz/. There is also annual national hackaton where winners from the regional ones compete: Hackathon veřejné správy 5.0 (hackujstat.cz).
Furthermore, the Ministry for Regional Development and the Ministry of Industry and Trade are collecting suggestions for opening data from users. The City of Brno, in turn, supports reuse by city hall employees by organizing internal workshops and training.

column2:
Have any public bodies in your country developed any systematic way of gathering reuse cases?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: How does the gathering happen?
column4: The National Open Data Team from the Digital and Information Agency every year carries out a survey among open data providers as a part of the open data impact measurement and the preparation of the Annual Report on the State of Open Data to monitor the re-use cases. Moreover, as shown from the regular annual survey between data providers, almost 10 providers (from 56 respondents) gather re-use cases or directly participate in the development of applications or portals working with their data.
column7:
The National Open Data Team from the Digital and Information Agency every year carries out a survey among open data providers as a part of the open data impact measurement and the preparation of the Annual Report on the State of Open Data to monitor the re-use cases. Moreover, as shown from the regular annual survey between data providers, almost 18 providers (from 65 respondents) gather re-use cases. 14 of the providers claim that they have initiated or participated in the development of applications or portals working with their data. 
Moreover, the National Open Data Team gathers reuse cases directly through national portal where users can register reuse cases, link them to used dataset registred in the portal and publish them in the catalogue of applications that is available th the portal itself at https://data.gov.cz/aplikace.

column2:
Are there any public bodies in your country that have developed a systematic ways of classifying the gathered reuse cases?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: According to which categories are reuse cases classified (e.g. by policy field)?
column4: The National Open Data Team from the Digital and Information Agency in the open data impact measurement classifies the re-use cases into the following categories: Information providing, New services and products,  Media portals and Others.
column7: The National Open Data Team from the Digital and Information Agency in the open data impact measurement classifies the re-use cases into the following categories: Information providing, New services and products,  Media portals and Others. There's also a thematic classification such as Government and public sector, Economy, Agriculture, Culture, Society, Environment etc. altogether 12 categories (from the European Vocabulary)  that is available at the catalogue of applications directly at the portal.

The methodology was updated in 2020 and now provides a more comprehensive impact assessment. The results of the study for the 2022 year are available online here: https://data.gov.cz/kodi/. However, thanks to the ongoing study, we have collected the re-use examples, see below.
column7: The Open Data team in previous years developed the methodology to follow and analyse the open data impact in CZ. Annually we conduct survey among the data providers as well as gather various data and information on the re-use to have the needed data for the annual report. This year's Impact Report Annual Report on the State of Open Data is still in process and will be available in the summer 2024.

In 2023 data journalist Jan Boček from the public radio Český Rozhlas published the first series of articles on his investigation of the illegal redistribution of drugs from the pharmacies across the CZ worth 20 million EUR. Most of the drugs ended up in the pharmacies abroad. This investigation was conducted based on analysing the open data of the State Institute of Drug Control which led to uncovering the whole illegal business. There were several steps taken to prevent this practice from the part of the Ministry of Health and penalties were given. Nevertheless, the case is not closed yet.

The Supreme Audit Office conducts an Annual Report that gives a complex overview of persistent systemic problems the Czech state faces. The Supreme Audit Office evaluates how successful the state is when solving these issues. The Office mainly uses open data for their controls made over the year in state offices and bodies. Eg. for the evaluation of the state of digitalization they use this dataset:  https://data.gov.cz/datov%C3%A1-sada?iri=https%3A%2F%2Fdata.gov.cz%2Fzdroj%2Fdatov%C3%A9-sady%2F17651921%2Ff50cfdd635e1c37698ebb9c50c881d4c.

column7: The Czech Society for Cardiology made a significant revision of the National Plan for Cardiology  (https://www.nzip.cz/clanek/1652-narodni-kardiovaskularni-plan) based on the prediction that was an outcome of the analysis of the available data. It seems that cardiovascular disease is not only a problem of bad lifestyle but is connected to a broader problem that the new plan reflects.  For the analysis, they used open datasets e.g. about the deaths caused by diseases of the circulatory system: https://www.nzip.cz/datova-sada/103

column7:
The Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs publishes the Social Exclusion Index (https://www.socialni-zaclenovani.cz/index_socialniho_vylouceni/) based on the analysis of (and not only) available open data. This determines the area where the activities of the Agency for Social Inclusion are concentrated, which ensures support in the process of social integration of residents at risk of social exclusion (three quarters of this population group is made up of the Roma minority). The agency creates local partnerships in identified localities, on which it targets aid, including, for example, advice on drawing funds from European structural funds. 
For example, the following datasets are used to calculate the index: https://data.mpsv.cz/web/data/nezamestnanost-v-obcich-od-brezna-2014, https://data.gov.cz/datov%C3%A1-sada?iri=https%3A%2F%2Fdata.gov.cz%2Fzdroj%2Fdatov%C3%A9-sady%2F70940517%2F1122955719, https://data.gov.cz/datov%C3%A1-sada?iri=https%3A%2F%2Fdata.gov.cz%2Fzdroj%2Fdatov%C3%A9-sady%2F66002222%2F16f5cf654712a7a6f1d789a6ee5662de.

column4:
There is currently a project called NERP - National Environmental Reporting Platformthat focuses on available sources of environmental data and tries to streamline their collection and processing and to analyze their impact on the social, political and legislative requirementscasued by the climate and environmental changes - https://nerp.cenia.cz/. The project will be finished in 2023.

The company Blindspot.si, which otherwise deals with e.g. the efficient use of space in transport containers or the optimisation of transport routes, used the election data of the Czech Statistical Office (https://www.volby.cz/opendata/opendata.htm ) in an innovative way to predict the presidential election results (https://volby.blindspot.ai/). The company wanted to test their model using artificial intelligence. Due to the high quality of the open data and the speed at which the Czech Statistical Office provides it, the voters had very precise election predictions at hand  instantly.

There is a non-profit organisation Czechitas that opens the world of IT to women. It educates them and helps them to change their careers. This organisation was a co-organiser of one of the regional hackatons in Brno that worked with the open data of the City of Brno.  https://www.czechitas.cz/hackuj-brno Czechitas also widely use the open data from the National Open Data Portal in their educational programmes.  
The consulting company Dun & Bradstreet (https://www.dnb.com/cs-cz/) uses a large amount of open data in its products, which helps clients from large and small and medium-sized enterprises gain a competitive advantage on the market. It offers, for example, a rating proving the economic stability of companies to ensure quality suppliers and customers, information on existing and potential business partners, reducing the outflow of customers, or ensuring credit risk monitoring in real time. Businesses thus prevent negative events and ensure growth. column7: Open data is also used by the Carbonfix online platform for calculating the carbon footprint of companies (https://www.carbonfix.cz/).
